Each band rides ON TOP of Battle Brothers' own fall of the shot a tile (the fight's shotLineOf), which stays as the library gives it. hit_by_tile: points added to the chance at exactly that many tiles; damage_by_tile: the share of the damage that arrives, a step (past the last tile listed the last share holds); line: a band's own fall a tile in place of the class's (base, per_tile, free tiles). PISTOL none: the thrown line already makes it best at one and two tiles (75 75 65 55 on a thug), NYPD hit rates fall the same way (RAND). SHOTGUN whole to two tiles, 0.6 at three, 0.35 at four: a cylinder bore's pattern opens about 0.6 inch a yard, every pellet on a torso to two tiles (a tile is a house, about 12 m), so the fall bites from a roof's extra tiles (rule 428(b)). RIFLE -10 at the next tile: handling, a long gun in a man's face (his 'range debuff'); best at two to five. SCOPE (weapons.json band 'scope', the scoped deer rifle; reach 8): its own line, +10 and -1 a tile past two, -20 at the next tile and -10 at two: the glass narrows the view close and holds the shot far (45 55 64 63 62 61 60 59 on a thug; TUNING's table words say +15, its own numbers are +10's). BOW -10 at the next tile: Battle Brothers lets no bow or crossbow shoot the next tile at all; rule 185 lets every weapon, so the bow takes the rifle's handling cut for the same reason (draft, a NOTE to TUNING). BOTTLES none: the thrown things start at two tiles (their rows' own minimum) on the thrown line. The storeys (COMBAT TWO, rule 428(b)) add reach and points and never multiply a band: the band reads the true distance in tiles.

A shove that puts him up there is not his climb. The zone of control's free swing and the free shot are on somebody else's turn and stand (Battle Brothers' rule, rules.json zone_of_control). Battle Brothers has no such rule: a climb there costs +1 AP a level (ap.move_cost.height_change_extra) and nothing else; ours is his. The AI: a shooter climbs only for the shot NEXT turn, never while he has a shot or a tile that gives one now.

auto_finds_a_shot.source: VAMILY.md rule 322 (Paolo 11/2, ask line 319); Battle Brothers' tactical AI (scripts/ai/tactical/behaviors/ai_engage_ranged.nut selectBestTargetTile(_entity, _maxRange, _considerLineOfFire, _visibleTileNeeded) and its PotentialDanger list: gist.github.com/Suor/82489e82556a81d51445bcd4717b3950); XCOM 2's movement profiles (tiles graded by cover, distance to enemies, flank shots, allies' line of sight: steamcommunity.com/workshop/filedetails/discussion/793861140/282992646973104300); records/BOHEMIA_COMBAT_HEIGHT_IS_ACCURACY_AND_AUTO_PLAYS_SMART_11_2_26.md
auto_finds_a_shot.quote: with auto combat you want the characters to get into places where they have the ability to hit the enemy... my sniper, my rifle character, ends his turn without trying to get to the best point of view, a place with line of sight where he can shoot
auto_finds_a_shot.why: COMBAT 4 11/2: AUTO's shooter with no shot from where he stands grades every tile he can walk to this turn. FIRST BY KIND, in order: shot_now, a tile he can shoot from THIS turn (the AP, the breath and the rounds left after the walk; range and line of sight the rules' own canStrike, on a man his side sees) that is not beside a club of theirs; shot_now_in_a_ring, the same beside a club of theirs (taken only when no other tile gives the shot: 'not stepping next to a melee enemy unless it must'; for a gun whose damage falls off with the distance, the shotgun, beside two of them: the one man's ring is where its shot is best, rule 187(d)); shot_next_turn, a tile not beside a club of theirs from which he would have the shot NEXT turn (a full turn's AP, the breath that comes back, the gun loaded), taken only when the tile he stands on gives no shot next turn either. A tile of none of these kinds is no vantage (he closes on the fight as before). THEN, among tiles of the same kind, in the brain's coin (hit chance points, the cap 95 a sure shot): his best shot from the tile, its chance (the +10 a storey up is in it) times the share of the damage his gun's range band gives at that distance (ours.range_bands: the shotgun's best tile is the next one), minus danger_per_foe for each club of theirs that could stand beside the tile next turn (its walk on the flat; a beast that cannot climb counts none at a roof tile with no ground beside it; Battle Brothers' PotentialDanger), plus safety_per_storey a storey up (their shots lose 10 a storey), plus cover_share of the cover's ranged defence on the tile (XCOM's cover), plus ap_spent a point of AP walked (the shorter walk on a tie). Never back to where an idle turn began (the undo veto, rule 176(b)); once he has shot this turn he walks only to shoot again (Battle Brothers' shooters do not creep after the shot). club_target_weight: AUTO's club choosing the tile to strike from adds this times the share of the man one blow takes (hit chance x the blow / his health and armour, at most 1: the weakest he can reach) for the best man from that tile, so he walks to the man he can drop, with the friends who surround him. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false.

Every side, his men and theirs; the preview lights the three on the aim (a ring armed before the aim is lit like an arc, every tile one of its aims would reach). auto_best_turn.source: VAMILY.md rule 332 (Paolo 11/2, ask line 331); records/BOHEMIA_COMBAT_AUTO_PLAYS_THE_BEST_TURN_AND_THE_ROUND_SWING_11_2_26.md; Battle Brothers' AI (ai_engage_ranged's PotentialDanger; the wiki's bb_all/0626_Developer Posts.txt, the AI picks the best target and tile behaviour by behaviour, one turn at a time); VAMILY rule 332 amended (Paolo 11/2, ask line 334, the coordinator's routine 'COMBAT 6: a turn's score counts the next turn')
auto_best_turn.quote: are we going to let auto combat use abilities... two offhand items you can bring... I don't want AI to prioritize finding the mechanic, then the melee guy has to go straight for the mechanic and dodge through all the robots... I don't need you to be the world's best chess simulator... the best course of action in that turn, to do the most damage and take the least damage within that turn
auto_best_turn.why: COMBAT 6 11/2: AUTO PLAYS THE BEST TURN for each man of his (the crew's switch best_turn, ai.json). Every time he acts it lists what he can do THIS turn: a blow on each man in reach, every sweep of his weapon on each man it can be aimed at, the active perks he carries (Rally, Rotation, Footwork, Recover, and at the turn's end Indomitable at its share of what is coming, Taunt for what it takes off a friend, Adrenaline at adrenaline_share of the kill it could make next round on a man who would otherwise swing at him first: priced as a share of any blow next turn it was spent nearly every turn and lost 3 more of 30 robot fights), a swap to a weapon in his bag (its AP: the library's 4, Quick Hands' first one free; at most swaps_a_turn) then that weapon's best blow from where he stands, the swap paying kit_next_turn of what the weapon left in his hands does worse next turn from where he stands (and a swap with nothing to hit now taken when the bag's weapon is the better one for next turn: the weapon he ends the turn holding is where the turn leaves him, like the tile), a walk then a blow or a sweep (a whip's lash from the second tile is a blow from that tile), a reload (then the shot if the AP is left; else reload_next_turn of next turn's shot), the cell vest's squeeze, and holding (a turn with nothing spent is the rest: 30 back, not 15). Each is scored in one coin, the hurt in health and armour: what it deals (hit chance x the blow at the weapon's middle, every man it strikes, each his own roll) plus, for every man it strikes, the road to his kill: the share of him it takes and what it adds to the chance he drops (with the blows the team still has to come on the named man) x what his death is worth a round (his blows and his lesson, deathWorth: the mechanic is worth his machines) x kill_rounds (rule 201's coin, so a blow on the mechanic in reach is worth more than a blow on a robot, and a man who gets up again is worth only what takes him under the raise); MINUS what he takes before his next turn on the tile he ends on: every man of theirs who can swing at that tile next turn (their walk on the flat and a blow; a man already beside another of ours keeps to his reach) or shoot it (his range), his chance there (the storeys and the cover are in it) x his blows x the blow, shared among the men of ours he could reach when danger_shared, less the chance this action drops or disarms him; and a man in a ring of theirs does not walk out of it through the free swings (Battle Brothers' own; Footwork is how he leaves, and with it the walk is weighed by the chance a free swing stops it). The best is taken. A blow beats holding whenever it hurts them at all; a walk to a blow is taken only when what it deals beats what it costs. NO MULTI-TURN PLANS: with no blow this turn he closes as before (the line, the shooter's tile, the roof), and a walk of chase_tiles tiles or more in his turn that ends where chase_reach or more of their clubs can swing at him next turn is never taken, to close or to strike, unless the blow at its end drops a man at kill_on_offer or better (the player plans the long chase, or a gambit he sets). OUT OF STAMINA: an action that would leave him unable to swing next turn (his breath after it, less the 15 that comes back, plus the breath their blows are expected to put on him before then where he ends (each blow's chance to land times fatigue.on_struck, a club's miss fatigue.on_dodge_or_block, shared as the hurt is, at most fatigue_from_them_between_turns), plus his blow, over his most) is dropped unless it drops a man at kill_on_offer or better (a kill on offer always wins); with nothing useful left he holds, which is the rest (Recover in its place when he carries it and it gives more back: his breath over 30). THE SQUEEZE (rule 305: the risk shown first, his button): AUTO squeezes only when the preview shows it burns none of his own men AND it drops falls_needed of theirs or more, or he is going down anyway before his next turn (what he takes there is more than his health left). His gambits first: taunted he swings at the man who called him. The mechanic is never chased: a blow on him scores highest of its own accord when it is on offer this turn (his death is worth his machines, rule 182's lesson); a walk to him through the robots pays for every robot that can swing at the tile. The climb rule stands (a tile his walk climbs a roof to gives no blow this turn). A swap at most swaps_a_turn a turn and moves_a_turn walks a turn so a turn always ends. rotation_margin: a Rotation must move rotation_margin of hurt off the pair; end_spend_floor: a spend at the turn's end must be worth this much. Drafts for TUNING, tuned:false. AMENDED 11/2 (rule 332 amended, ask line 334, Paolo: 'how does the auto turn know that climbing a roof is what's best this turn if they are a ranged character... and that should apply to enemies with guns as well... how do they know the best place to climb, even if it doesn't benefit them the most this turn, that investment of a higher roof... compared to maybe taking a breath so you can make a triple swing next turn'): THIS TURN PLUS ONE DISCOUNTED NEXT TURN, never deeper. Every option is worth what it does this turn PLUS next_turn x the best one action his next turn can be from the tile and the state it leaves him in (the weapon in his hands, the gun loaded or not, the breath he will have: after the action, less the 15 back, or the rest's 30, plus what their blows put on him), against their men where they stand now: the shot from a roof carries its storeys' hit and range, the swing carries the breath to afford it. next_turn 0.6 [COMBAT 6's draft, TUNING's]: next turn counts for a bit over half of this one because they move and things change before it comes (a man of theirs walks out of the shot, another walks into it, the named man may already be down); at 1 a promise would weigh as much as a blow landed now, at 0 nothing ever climbs or rests for a bigger swing (a climb ends his attacks, rule 328). WHERE TO CLIMB: every roof his walk climbs onto this turn is an option (no blow now, rule 328), worth what his next turn can do from it less what he takes up there (a wolf cannot climb, rule 321; a club swings up from beside it at -10 a storey); the best roof wins only when it beats shooting now from the ground and holding. REST FOR THE SWING: holding is scored the same way (nothing now, the breath back, then the best next turn: a sweep on the men lined up in front of him) against striking now. theirs: the same brain plays their shooters and swingers, after their own lessons (the hook, the net, the scream, Battle Brothers' climb for a shooter with no shot), with Battle Brothers' spread on their blows (201(e)); with nothing to hit, or holding beating every option for any reason but the rest for a bigger swing, they walk their own way (their rush, their line); no long-chase veto for them (Battle Brothers' men charge). weighed_kept: the best options kept on the man with his pick (u.btLast, for the probe and the gate; nothing he feels). The probe logs each pick's reason (u.btSay, e.g. 'climbs: next turn 34 from the roof x0.6 = 20 ... beats strike 12 now').

endgame_light.why: WEIGHT IS NOT QUALITY (rule 377(d), his words: 'maybe an endgame light armor is better than most of the heavy armor'). Battle Brothers' own named light pieces do not do it (its best, the Named Noble Mail, holds 176 to 200 at 8 to 12; its Wolf Helmet 154 to 175 at 4 to 7): THE FUTURE DOES (rule 32: the game starts in the ruin and gets reclaimed, techy, modern). Realism first: an ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene rifle plate weighs about a third of a steel plate that stops the same round (about 1.3 kg against 3.8 kg for a 10 by 12 inch plate) and a modern helmet about 1.4 kg against 2 to 4 kg of a steel great helm. Each piece is a champion's drop (Battle Brothers' champions 'always have a named item', bb_all/0363) and costs what its named medium costs; never on the shelf (shelf false). A body and a helmet together weigh 12: a LIGHT man who walks free and holds more than most heavy men. NOT IN THE FIGHT YET: no champion drops a named item in our code (COMBAT 7's); the rows are shaped like armor.json rows so the drop can hand one straight to bodyRow and headRow.

breath_floor.why: AMENDED 11/10 BY COMBAT TWO (VAMILY rule 435(e), ask line 556, Paolo: 'one of my guys keeps saying he's winded and he doesn't move and he doesn't attack, but I can move him myself'): READ BY THE FIGHT NOW (fatMax's floor for a man of his, his own blow x strikes), and 2 where it was 1: at 1 the heaviest kit left him one blow from fresh, so he swung, was winded, rested a turn, swung, rested (half his turns WINDED); at 2 a turn's 15 gives a blow of 15 or less back every turn, so no kit leaves him winded turn after turn. Measured on every origin's start crew (12 rolls each): no man is held up by it (the floor bites only in the heaviest bought kit); his card says HEAVY KIT: BREATH HELD AT n when it does. TUNING's to tune. WAS: NEVER A SWING, THE BREATH HALF (rule 377(c), his words: 'please make sure this does not make it impossible to do any sort of attack or abilities'). Battle Brothers takes armour weight off a man's breath too (Max. Fatigue; the fight's gearFat), and with the walk now costing the heaviest a tile that second cost can still stop a swing: MEASURED (the fight headless, 11/3), a sellsword (93 breath) in a coat of plates and a full helm (62) holding a two-handed hammer has 13 breath for a 15-breath strike, so he can never swing it; with the other two-handers 17, one swing a turn; Rally and Indomitable (25 each, bb_all/1633, 1076) never. THE NUMBER: whatever he wears, his breath pool holds at least his dearest strike or active ability this many times from fresh (1). The heaviest still tires him fast (Battle Brothers' cost, kept): it never makes a swing impossible.
